title: Understanding the Loss Function
text: The loss function is a measure of how well the model's predictions match the actual outcomes. It is given by:\n\nL(theta_0,theta_1)=1/n*sum{i=1}{n}{(y_i-theta_0/x_i-log{theta_1}x_i+theta_0*theta_1*(x_i**2+1))}

title: Gradient Vector Components
text: The gradient vector provides the direction and rate of change of the loss function with respect to the parameters $$\theta_0$$ and $$\theta_1$$. It is given by:\n\npartial{L}/partial{theta}=(1/n*sum{i=1}{n}{(-1/x_i+theta_1*x_i**2+theta_1)},1/n*sum{i=1}{n}{(-x_i/theta_1+theta_0*x_i**2+theta_0)})

hintAnswer: Initial weights can affect convergence speed and whether the algorithm finds the global minimum.
title: Impact of Initial Weights
text: Consider how the initial values of $$\theta_0$$ and $$\theta_1$$ might affect the convergence of the gradient descent algorithm. What happens if they are too large or too small?

title: Convergence to Optimal Weights
text: The choice of initial weights can determine if the gradient descent algorithm converges to the true optimal weights or gets stuck in a local minimum.
